# Controlled content reuse {#sec-content-reuse}

Repeated prose should have one reviewable source without turning a manuscript
into a maze of hidden includes. Each specimen below names a registered fragment,
a persistent use-site identity, its permitted context, and every substitution.
The rendered text remains ordinary semantic content in HTML, EPUB, Typst, and
LuaLaTeX.

## Shared notice {#sec-reuse-notice}

{{< alk-reuse reuse-safety-disconnect id="reuse-use-safety-disconnect" context="chapter" equipment="the test fixture" >}}

The source registry makes this safety dependency visible before rendering. A
book may change the equipment name, but it cannot silently alter the reviewed
instructions or nest another reusable fragment inside them.

## Shared definition {#sec-reuse-definition}

{{< alk-reuse reuse-observed-value-definition id="reuse-use-observed-value-definition" context="chapter" term="Observed value" >}}

A reusable definition is appropriate when several chapters need identical
wording. Glossary entries remain in the glossary registry; this mechanism is
for a complete prose block placed in the reading flow.

## Shared legal and editorial text {#sec-reuse-legal}

{{< alk-reuse reuse-rights-review id="reuse-use-rights-review" context="chapter" book_title="Alkahest Reference Book" rights_holder="the responsible publisher" >}}

Legal or rights-related fragments are versioned and checksummed so a review can
name the exact text it approved. Parameters personalize facts; they do not
permit arbitrary edits to the controlled wording.

## Shared worked example {#sec-reuse-example}

{{< alk-reuse reuse-tolerance-example id="reuse-use-tolerance-example" context="chapter" nominal_voltage="3.3" tolerance_percent="5" lower_voltage="3.135" upper_voltage="3.465" >}}

Values are explicit at the use site. The reusable fragment supplies the stable
explanation and editorial distinctions, while the chapter owns the example's
inputs.

## Shared project prerequisites {#sec-reuse-project-prerequisites}

{{< alk-reuse reuse-project-prerequisites id="reuse-use-project-prerequisites" context="project" required_skill="basic voltage measurement" required_equipment="a current-limited supply and multimeter" safety_review="disconnect-before-changing-connections" >}}

The project context is part of the checked call. Moving this fragment into an
unsupported front-matter or legal context fails source validation instead of
quietly changing its meaning.

## Dependency boundary {#sec-reuse-boundary}

Reusable files are local, backend-neutral Markdown with no headings, persistent
IDs, raw backend commands, or nested reuse calls. Cross-book text must be
vendored or supplied by an explicitly versioned engine release in a future
multi-book workflow; direct paths into another book are never valid sources.
